TALLAHASSEE --- Heading into the next legislative term, incoming House Speaker Sam Garrison is setting up new committees, including one to look into artificial intelligence and other new technologies.

The Fleming Island Republican wrote in a memo to members this week he’s creating a Policy & Strategy Committee and replacing the Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee with the Advanced Technology & Digital Security Committee.

By focusing on state technology governance and modernization, the intent of the Advanced Technology committee is “to make informed decisions about technology to prevent costly failures,” Garrison wrote.

“It will also cover artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, cybersecurity, digital privacy, data governance, and critical infrastructure security,” Garrison stated. “These issues affect both state government and the Floridians and businesses that rely on technology every day.”

Earlier this year the House rejected Gov. Ron DeSantis’ proposal to protect consumers’ interactions with artificial intelligence with new regulations.

Former House Speaker Daniel Perez, now the U.S. ambassador to Brazil, maintained the federal government should handle the issue.

Also, Garrison tapped Lakeland Republican Rep. Jennifer Canady to lead the Policy & Strategy Committee, which is to consider long range planning.

“I want the House to consider where Florida needs to be in five or 10 or 20 years and what steps we should take now to get there,” Garrison wrote.

Garrison also reestablished the Public Integrity Committee to consider “issues like lobbying, financial disclosure, and conflicts of interest.”

In addition to Canady, Garrison on Monday named several other Republicans to leadership roles. Tampa Rep. Traci Koster is chairwoman of the Appropriations Committee, Dade City Rep. Randy Maggard is majority leader, and Coral Gables Rep. Demi Busatta is speaker pro tempore and chairwoman of the Health & Human Services Committee.

Other committee leaders include: Rep. Adam Botana, R-Bonita Springs, chairman of the Rules & Calendar Committee; Rep. Fiona McFarland, R-Sarasota, chairwoman of the Education & Employment Committee; Rep. Mike Redondo, R-Miami, chairman of the Health Care Appropriations Subcommittee; Rep. Jason Shoaf, R-Port St. Joe, chairman of the Commerce Committee; Rep. John Snyder, R-Stuart, chairman of the State Affairs Committee; and Rep. Kaylee Tuck, R-Lake Placid, chairwoman of the Judiciary Committee.

The Legislature will convene an organizational session Tuesday, when Garrison and Senate President-designate Jim Boyd, R-Bradenton, will formally begin their new roles.
